# Results — Study 906 (EM Local Bonds, FX-Hedged — a proxy)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: EM
**local-currency** bonds (EMLC) pay a fat local rate that the currency swings drown, so
**stripping the FX** should leave a real, harvestable local-rate carry vs USD-EM debt (EMB)
and cash. Because no clean FX-hedged EM-local ETF exists on US tape, the "hedge" is a
**long-UUP (dollar-index) overlay proxy** — it tracks the developed-market DXY basket, NOT
the EMLC currency basket, so it strips only *part* of the EM-FX. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
Numbers are as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `32605dae0c9c` (total-return closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, **total-return**), cached as parquet under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Tickers | **EMLC** (VanEck local-EM, 2010-08+), **LEMB** (iShares local-EM, 2011-11+), **EBND** (SPDR local-EM, 2011-03+), **EMB** (iShares **USD**-EM = bench), **UUP** (DB dollar-bull = overlay), **BIL** (1-3m T-bill = cash) |
| Frequency | month-end simple total returns; final partial month dropped |
| Hedge | variance-min ratio `b = cov(EMLC−BIL, UUP−BIL)/var(UUP−BIL)`; hedged excess `= (EMLC−BIL) − b·(UUP−BIL)`. `b<0` ⇒ a **long-UUP** overlay. In-sample `b` (an FX-strip **upper bound**); a 36-month walk-forward `b` (lag 1) is the implementable cross-check |
| Race | **excess-vs-excess** (every leg minus BIL): unhedged EMLC vs hedged-EMLC vs USD-EM (EMB) vs cash |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the hedged excess and on the hedged−EMB premium; circular-block bootstrap Sharpe CI; a two-era cut (2021-01-01); a costed overlay; a planted-carry synthetic control |

**Proxy — named on the Signal axis.** UUP is long USD vs EUR/JPY/GBP/CAD/SEK/CHF (the DXY
basket), not BRL/MXN/IDR/ZAR/THB (the EMLC basket). It explains ~**50 %** of EMLC's
variance (β = −1.12, HAC *t* = −11.9), so the overlay strips the *systematic* dollar move
but leaves a residual idiosyncratic EM-FX beta (≈ **+0.10** on the walk-forward hedge). The
"hedge" is deliberately imperfect and every number carries that caveat.

## The headline — does the FX-strip leave a real local carry? (EMLC)

n = **191** months, 2010-08 → 2026-06, excess-of-cash:

| leg (excess of BIL) | excess ann. | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **unhedged EMLC** | +0.33 %/yr | +0.03 | +0.14 |
| **hedged EMLC** (UUP overlay) | **+1.62 %/yr** | **+0.20** | **+0.94** |
| **EMB** (USD-EM, the sibling) | +3.10 %/yr | +0.34 | +1.48 |
| hedged − EMB premium | **−1.48 %/yr** | — | **−0.81** (Welch −0.49) |

The **mechanical FX-strip is real**: raw EMLC earns essentially nothing over cash (Sharpe
+0.03 — the currency drowns the local rate), and stripping the dollar move lifts the excess
to +1.62 %/yr and the Sharpe to +0.20, cutting the drawdown from −32 % to −17 % (below).
**But the residual local carry is not statistically real** (HAC *t* = +0.94) and it **loses
to simply owning EMB** (the hedged−EMB premium is *negative*). The claimed "harvestable
local-rate carry vs USD-EM debt and bills" fails the robust bar on both legs.

Independent confirms — the same picture on the other two local-EM ETFs:

| local ETF | unhedged Sharpe | hedged Sharpe (HAC *t*) | hedged − EMB |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| LEMB (2011-11+) | −0.02 | +0.23 (*t* +0.99) | −1.03 %/yr |
| EBND (2011-03+) | +0.00 | +0.26 (*t* +1.16) | −1.33 %/yr |

## Bootstrap Sharpe CI (circular block, excess-of-cash)

| leg | Sharpe | 95 % CI | frac < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| unhedged EMLC | +0.03 | [−0.38, +0.47] | 0.44 |
| **hedged EMLC** | **+0.20** | **[−0.21, +0.69]** | 0.17 |
| EMB (USD-EM) | +0.39 | [−0.05, +0.91] | 0.04 |

The hedged-EMLC Sharpe CI **straddles zero** — the local carry it reveals is not
distinguishable from noise. Even EMB, the better leg, barely clears.

## Walk-forward hedge (36m rolling `b`, lag 1 — the implementable version)

No in-sample `b`, no look-ahead: excess **+1.60 %/yr**, Sharpe **+0.20**, HAC *t* **+0.79**
(n = 167, 2012-08 → 2026-06). The DXY proxy leaves a **residual EM-FX beta of +0.10**
(R² 0.01) — so the in-sample-`b` result is not flattered by look-ahead; the effect is
simply thin.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2021-01-01)

| era | hedged excess | HAC *t* | prem vs EMB | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-08 → 2020-12 (n=125) | +1.76 %/yr | +0.70 | −3.58 %/yr | −1.87 |
| 2021-01 → 2026-06 (n=66) | +1.34 %/yr | +0.84 | +2.50 %/yr | +0.71 |

The hedged carry keeps the same (positive, insignificant) sign in both eras — it is not one
era's artefact, but it never clears *t* ≥ 2 in either, and it only stops *losing* to EMB in
the post-2021 high-rate era (still not significantly winning).

## Drawdown (total-return NAV) — where the hedge genuinely helps

| series | max drawdown | window |
|---|--:|---|
| EMLC (unhedged) | **−32.3 %** | 2013-05 → 2022-10 |
| EMB (USD-EM) | −28.7 % | 2021-09 → 2022-10 |
| **hedged EMLC** | **−17.1 %** | 2013-04 → 2015-09 |

The FX-strip roughly **halves** the drawdown — a genuine, mechanical **diversification**
benefit, even though it does not translate into a significant *return* premium.

## The timer — cost the overlay

Re-strike the UUP overlay monthly to `|b|`·NAV notional at a 3 bp one-way spread + light
local-ETF maintenance:

| | value |
|---|--:|
| hedge `b` | −1.118 |
| overlay + maintenance charge | 0.46 %/yr |
| gross hedged excess | +1.62 %/yr |
| **net hedged excess** | **+1.15 %/yr** (HAC *t* +0.67, Sharpe +0.15) |
| **net premium vs EMB** | **−1.95 %/yr** (HAC *t* −1.07) |

Even *gross* the hedged carry loses to just holding EMB; the overlay cost only widens the
gap. There is no bankable local-rate edge here — the simpler USD-EM ETF dominates.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic monthly world: a planted **local-minus-US** differential under a DXY-explained
FX drag plus a residual FX the proxy can't reach. No network.

| world | hedged excess | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| planted (carry = 4 %/yr, seed 906) | +5.53 %/yr | **+3.25** |
| null (carry = 0), **20 seeds** | — | mean **−0.01** (sd 1.41), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20** |

The detector recovers a *planted* local carry cleanly and fires on ~1/20 nulls (the nominal
false-positive rate) — so the thin real-tape result is a true "small edge", not a biased
estimator. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The FX-strip is **mechanically real and correctly signed**: EMLC's
  return is ~50 % dollar-basket FX (β = −1.12, HAC *t* = −11.9), stripping it lifts the
  excess-of-cash Sharpe from +0.03 to +0.20 and halves the drawdown (−32 % → −17 %),
  consistently across EMLC/LEMB/EBND. **But the residual local-rate carry is not a robust
  premium**: +1.62 %/yr at HAC *t* = +0.94, a bootstrap Sharpe CI of [−0.21, +0.69] that
  straddles zero, and — the decisive leg — it **loses to simply owning USD-EM debt** (the
  hedged − EMB premium is −1.48 %/yr, *t* = −0.81). Real mechanism, no harvestable edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even gross, the hedged local carry (Sharpe +0.20) is dominated
  by the plain USD-EM sibling EMB (Sharpe +0.39); after the UUP-overlay re-strike cost
  (0.46 %/yr) the net is +1.15 %/yr (*t* +0.67) and the net premium vs EMB is −1.95 %/yr.
  The apparent "local-hedged edge" is a mirage — a simpler, cheaper ETF wins outright.
